name: Geranium 'Rozanne'
desc: Long-flowering hardy geranium with violet-blue flowers and white centres, ground-covering habit
note: Universal performer across all Home Counties soils, including clay

name: Alchemilla mollis
desc: Frothy lime-green flowers above pleated leaves that hold raindrops
note: Tolerant ground-cover that thrives in any Home Counties garden

name: Hellebore
desc: Nodding cup-shaped flowers in shades of pink, purple and white above evergreen leaves
note: Reliable winter-into-spring colour for Bucks woodland-edge planting

name: Lavender 'Hidcote'
desc: Compact lavender with deep purple flower spikes and silver-grey aromatic foliage
note: Iconic chalk and sand performer; struggles on heavy wet clay

name: Foxglove
desc: Tall spikes of tubular pink-purple bell flowers with spotted throats; biennial that self-sows
note: Self-seeds readily into shaded Home Counties borders

name: Catmint
desc: Cushion of soft blue flower spikes above grey-green aromatic leaves
note: Long-flowering pollinator magnet that thrives in Chilterns chalk

name: Salvia 'Caradonna'
desc: Upright spikes of deep violet flowers held on near-black stems
note: Modern border classic; long-flowering on Home Counties chalk and loam

name: Rudbeckia 'Goldsturm'
desc: Golden-yellow daisies with prominent dark cone centres, clump-forming
note: Late-summer workhorse for Home Counties clay borders

name: Japanese anemone
desc: Pale pink single flowers on tall wiry stems flowering in late summer to autumn
note: Reliable late-season colour for shaded Bucks and Herts gardens

name: Hydrangea 'Annabelle'
desc: Massive white mophead flowers on arching stems above bright green leaves
note: Clay and shade icon; flowers reliably even on heavy Home Counties soils

name: Rosa 'Gertrude Jekyll'
desc: Strongly fragrant rosette-shaped pink English rose, almost continuous flowering
note: David Austin classic; performs strongly on Home Counties clay loam

name: Verbena bonariensis
desc: Tall wiry stems bearing clusters of small purple flowers; airy see-through habit
note: Self-seeds reliably; H4 borderline but regenerates from seed each spring

name: Buddleja 'Black Knight'
desc: Long arching stems with deep purple cone-shaped flower spikes
note: Butterfly magnet; tolerant of all Home Counties soils

name: Nepeta 'Walker's Low'
desc: Soft mound of lavender-blue flower spikes above grey-green aromatic foliage
note: Best pollinator catmint; copes brilliantly with chalk

name: Heuchera 'Palace Purple'
desc: Mound of bronze-purple palmate leaves with delicate white flower sprays
note: Evergreen foliage interest year-round; works in pots and shaded borders

name: Hosta 'Sum and Substance'
desc: Massive chartreuse-yellow heart-shaped leaves forming statement clumps
note: Shade architecture; tolerates more sun than most hostas

name: Hakonechloa 'Aureola'
desc: Arching mound of golden-striped grass foliage with cascading habit
note: Best ornamental grass for shaded Home Counties gardens

name: Stipa tenuissima
desc: Fine silky grass with feathery golden flower plumes that move in the breeze
note: Climate-resilient grass that thrives on chalk and free-draining soils

name: Miscanthus 'Morning Light'
desc: Upright clump of narrow silver-edged grass leaves with pink-silver autumn plumes
note: Climate-resilient grass with strong winter silhouette and stems

name: Brunnera 'Jack Frost'
desc: Heart-shaped silver-frosted leaves with sky-blue forget-me-not flowers in spring
note: Lights up shaded Home Counties woodland borders

name: Bergenia
desc: Large round glossy evergreen leaves with clusters of pink or white spring flowers
note: Bombproof clay-and-shade plant; foliage reddens in winter

name: Astrantia major
desc: Delicate pincushion flowers surrounded by papery star-shaped bracts
note: Pollinator favourite for moist Home Counties clay-shade

name: Iris sibirica
desc: Slender purple-blue iris flowers with yellow throats above grass-like foliage
note: Climate-resilient iris that tolerates wet clay better than bearded irises

name: Daffodil 'Tête-à-tête'
desc: Compact dwarf daffodil with multiple bright golden-yellow trumpet flowers per stem
note: Toxic to deer and squirrels; perfect for pots and naturalising

name: Euphorbia characias
desc: Architectural evergreen with blue-grey leaves and acid yellow-green bract heads
note: Mediterranean specialist for sheltered chalk borders; H4 borderline

name: Daylily
desc: Trumpet-shaped flowers in oranges, yellows and reds above arching strap-like leaves
note: Climate-resilient daylilies cope with Home Counties drought and clay equally well

name: Physocarpus 'Diabolo'
desc: Large shrub with deep purple-bronze maple-shaped leaves and pink-white flower clusters
note: Climate-resilient purple-leaved foliage shrub for Home Counties statement planting

name: Viburnum opulus
desc: Native guelder rose with white lacecap flowers and translucent red autumn berries
note: UK native shrub; thrives on Home Counties clay and supports wildlife

name: Rosa rugosa
desc: Tough hedging rose with magenta single flowers, wrinkled leaves and large red hips
note: Most forgiving rose for any Home Counties soil; thorns deter deer

name: Rowan
desc: Native small tree with pinnate leaves, white spring flowers and bright red autumn berries
note: Native climate-resilient tree for Home Counties wildlife gardens

name: Amelanchier
desc: Multi-stemmed small tree with white spring blossom, bronze new leaves, fiery autumn colour
note: Four-season tree; one of the most reliable small trees for Home Counties

name: Calamagrostis 'Karl Foerster'
desc: Strictly upright pillar of narrow grass with feathery golden flower plumes
note: Climate-resilient feather-reed grass that holds vertical structure into winter

name: Sedum 'Autumn Joy'
desc: Flat rose-pink flowerheads on succulent grey-green stems, deepening to copper
note: Drought-tolerant late-season pollinator for sunny Home Counties borders

name: Echinacea 'Magnus'
desc: Large pink-purple daisy flowers with prominent orange-brown cone centres
note: Climate-resilient prairie pollinator; struggles in heavy wet clay

name: Achillea 'Moonshine'
desc: Flat lemon-yellow flowerheads above silver-grey feathery foliage
note: Drought-tolerant silver-leaved performer for chalk and gravel gardens

name: Helenium 'Moerheim Beauty'
desc: Rich copper-red daisy flowers with dark brown cone centres
note: Late-summer workhorse for Home Counties clay borders

name: Salvia yangii
desc: Silver-stemmed upright spires of small lavender-blue flowers with aromatic foliage
note: Russian sage by another name; reclassified to Salvia in 2017

name: Stachys byzantina
desc: Silver-grey felted leaves forming a soft fuzzy carpet, occasional pink flower spikes
note: Drought-tolerant ground cover; rots in heavy wet winter clay

name: Persicaria 'Firetail'
desc: Tall wiry stems with narrow deep red bottlebrush flower spikes
note: Climate-resilient long-flowerer for moist Home Counties clay

name: Christmas rose
desc: Pure white cup-shaped flowers with golden centres opening in deepest winter
note: True winter-flowering hellebore for Home Counties; needs sheltered position

name: Sarcococca
desc: Compact evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves and tiny intensely fragrant white winter flowers
note: Winter scent for shaded Home Counties paths and entrances

name: Cornus 'Midwinter Fire'
desc: Bare winter stems blazing in fiery orange-red-yellow tones, flame effect against winter light
note: Cut hard in spring for strongest winter stem colour

name: Cornus alba 'Sibirica'
desc: Thicket of bare vivid red dogwood stems creating winter drama
note: Tolerates wetter ground than 'Midwinter Fire'; brightest red stems

name: Mahonia 'Charity'
desc: Architectural evergreen with holly-like leaves and upright fragrant yellow winter flower spikes
note: Critical winter forage for early-emerging bumblebees in Home Counties

name: Winter jasmine
desc: Cascading bare green stems studded with bright yellow star flowers in deep winter
note: Winter colour for north-facing walls and banks; deserves training

name: Viburnum x bodnantense 'Dawn'
desc: Bare stems carrying clusters of fragrant pink tubular flowers all winter
note: Premier winter-fragrant shrub; plant near paths to enjoy the scent

name: Snowdrop
desc: Nodding white bell flowers with green markings on slim stems, emerging through winter
note: Earliest winter bulb; toxic so unbothered by deer or squirrels

name: Himalayan birch
desc: Small tree with brilliant white peeling papery bark glowing through winter
note: Best small winter-bark tree for Home Counties; effective in groups of three

name: Skimmia japonica
desc: Compact evergreen with glossy leaves, white spring flowers, female plants bear red berries
note: Acid-loving but tolerates loam with organic matter; struggles on solid chalk

name: Centranthus ruber
desc: Clusters of deep pink-red tubular flowers on upright grey-green stems
note: Self-seeds into walls and gravel; thrives on Chilterns chalk

name: Erigeron karvinskianus
desc: Mass of tiny white-and-pink daisies tumbling over walls and into paving cracks
note: Self-seeds into walls and crevices; flowers May to first frosts

name: Crocus 'Ruby Giant'
desc: Vibrant ruby-purple crocus flowers opening to reveal orange stamens
note: Early bee forage; naturalises into lawns better than other crocuses

name: Allium 'Purple Sensation'
desc: Perfect spherical purple flower heads on tall straight stems above strappy leaves
note: Architectural late-spring structure; bulbs unbothered by deer

name: Male fern
desc: Upright shuttlecock of bright green lacy fern fronds; deciduous in cold winters
note: Dry-shade essential for Home Counties woodland edges

name: Epimedium
desc: Delicate pink-and-yellow flowers on wiry stems above heart-shaped leaves
note: Dry-shade ground cover; tougher than it looks

name: Choisya 'Aztec Pearl'
desc: Evergreen shrub with narrow glossy aromatic leaves and clusters of fragrant white flowers
note: Often re-flowers in late summer; site sheltered for best results in Bucks

name: Viburnum tinus
desc: Evergreen shrub with pink buds opening to white flowers through winter and early spring
note: Bombproof evergreen; watch for viburnum beetle damage to leaves

name: Pulmonaria 'Blue Ensign'
desc: Deep gentian-blue flowers above plain dark green lungwort leaves; early spring bee forage
note: Critical early pollinator for emerging queen bumblebees in shade

name: Tulip 'Queen of Night'
desc: Elegant deep maroon-black single tulip flowers on tall stems
note: Plant late (Nov-Dec) for best results; treat as annual on heavy clay

name: Aster 'Mönch'
desc: Lavender-blue daisies with golden centres, outstandingly long-flowering
note: Mildew-resistant aster filling the late-autumn pollinator gap

name: Clematis 'Étoile Violette'
desc: Vigorous deciduous climber producing masses of nodding deep violet-purple flowers with creamy yellow centres in summer
note: Wilt-resistant viticella climber that performs reliably across the Home Counties; brilliant scrambling through climbing roses

name: Native honeysuckle
desc: UK native climber with fragrant tubular cream-and-pink flowers attractive to bees, butterflies and night-flying moths
note: Best with roots in shade and top growing into sun; one of the highest-value pollinator climbers for Home Counties wildlife gardens

name: Climbing hydrangea
desc: Self-clinging deciduous climber with lacy white lacecap flowers in early summer above heart-shaped foliage that turns gold in autumn
note: The shade-climber answer; ideal for north and east-facing Home Counties walls where little else thrives

name: Hart's tongue fern
desc: Native evergreen fern forming rosettes of glossy strap-shaped fronds, particularly happy on chalk
note: Bombproof shade plant for Chilterns chalk; tolerates dry shade once established

name: Soft shield fern
desc: Native evergreen fern with soft lacy fronds in graceful shuttlecock-shaped rosettes
note: Architectural counterpart to Male fern; works with hostas and pulmonarias in moist shaded borders

name: Knautia macedonica
desc: Crimson pincushion flowers on slender wiry stems above clump-forming foliage, flowering for months
note: Fills the long-flowering pollinator gap between summer salvias and autumn asters; needs sharp drainage on heavy Bucks clay

name: Aquilegia
desc: Cottage classic with nodding bonnet-shaped flowers in pinks, blues and purples above ferny foliage
note: Self-seeds beautifully into Home Counties cottage borders; cross-pollinates between cultivars producing surprise colours

name: Acanthus mollis
desc: Architectural perennial with large glossy lobed leaves and tall spikes of white flowers in dusky purple bracts
note: Drama for the Chilterns chalk border; site carefully as it returns from deep roots and is hard to remove

name: Tufted hair grass
desc: UK native semi-evergreen grass forming dense tussocks topped with airy clouds of golden-purple flower panicles in summer
note: UK native grass; airy summer panicles persist into winter; one of few ornamental grasses happy in partial shade

name: Crab apple 'Évereste'
desc: Compact ornamental tree with white spring blossom from scarlet buds, followed by orange-red autumn fruits persisting into winter
note: The four-season small tree for Home Counties suburban gardens; tolerates clay, chalk and pollution equally well
